title: Run plan proposal
description: What the Orchestrator returns: an ordered list of skill invocations and the edges between them, and nothing else. No property anywhere in this schema is numeric - not a value, not a confidence, not a timeout, not a loop ceiling. A plan is data about which skills run in what order; every number that governs a run comes from the constraint registry, the recipe defaults and the resolved scope, so a proposal cannot ask for another iteration, a longer timeout, a different model or a looser guard. Nor does it name an output contract: the code pins that from the skill. The proposal is turned into a recipe and put through the same compiler and the same plan assertions as a named one, and is used only if it survives both.

match.description: Categorical rather than a confidence score, deliberately. 'recipe' says a named recipe is the shape of this job; 'composed' says none is and these steps are; 'none' says the orchestrator cannot route this job, which is the case Triage exists for. A number here would invite a threshold nobody agreed, and a threshold is a policy decision rather than a model's.

recipe.description: The named recipe this plan is, when match is 'recipe'. The recipe is loaded from disk by name and its own steps are used; the proposal's steps are then a statement of what it believes that recipe does, which the compiler will disagree with if it is wrong.

rationale.description: Why this shape, in prose, for the person reading the run plan before it runs. Recorded in the run plan artifact; it decides nothing.

escalation_reason.description: Why nothing fits, when match is 'none'. Routed to Triage and from there to a person.

steps.description: The ordered list. Order is the topology the compiler derives from 'needs'; this array's order is not itself meaningful, which is why a step may name any other step it depends on.

skill.description: A name from the Skill Index and nothing else. Not a version: the resolved scope decides which version this engagement has, and a proposal naming one would be choosing a version it cannot see.

run_inputs.description: What this step takes from outside the plan, by the names the job manifest listed. Anything else is refused by the compiler: nothing enters a plan undeclared.
